candidates.title: Quote and work-order preparation for repair shops

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare quotes and work orders, handle invoicing, and order spare parts for a vehicle repair business.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Du tar fram offerter och arbetsorder, hantera fakturering och beställer reservdelar

ease.reason: A fictional quote-to-work-order tracker is a plausible small start, but the vacancy names no software or data format.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a repair shop may value help with quote and parts administration; this human vacancy proves no AI-service demand.

feasibility.reason: A two-week mock could draft fields for quotes, work orders and parts; live garage systems and accurate pricing are unshown.

autonomy.reason: Extracting fields and preparing a queue could repeat, while staff must verify pricing, parts and every order.

evidence.reason: The paid vacancy explicitly lists quotes, work orders, invoicing and parts orders, but gives no frequency or automation evidence.

candidates.reason: Assessed as the clearest bounded repair-administration chore among the selected leads. The ratings average below the threshold because the notice establishes human work but not a tested AI workflow, task frequency, or AI-service demand.

rejected.title: Quote and work-order preparation for repair shops
rejected.reason: Below threshold (mean 4.4): this fresh notice establishes repair-shop quote, work-order, invoice and parts administration, but no repeated task frequency, software access, working AI tool or demand for an AI service.

rejected.title: Time reports, invoicing and customer follow-up
rejected.reason: Previously assessed and below threshold; fresh text repeats time reports and invoicing, while customer follow-up and owner metrics lack a bounded automation specification. It does not establish AI-service demand.

rejected.title: Document registration and report preparation
rejected.reason: Explicit duties are document handling, registration, archiving, reports and system updates, but the notice gives no narrow workflow inputs, frequency or tool access; prior assessment was below threshold.

rejected.title: Project and case administration
rejected.reason: The notice describes broad project and case support without a specific bounded repeated task; this URL was already refused below threshold.

rejected.title: Unspecified administrator responsibilities
rejected.reason: The text ends after saying the administrator handles several areas and names no actual chore, so a useful task-specific design would require invention.

rejected.title: Meeting, annual-calendar and invoice administration
rejected.reason: This earlier notice was already refused; it lists meeting booking, annual-calendar updates and some invoice administration but does not establish a distinct supported AI workflow or AI-service demand.

rejected.title: Case registration and document coordination
rejected.reason: The notice lists records, archiving and broad coordination/statistics duties but does not bound inputs or a repeatable student workflow; previously assessed below threshold.

rejected.title: Student reception and substitute coordination
rejected.reason: The listed work includes reception, student administration and substitute sourcing; prior below-threshold assessment and any real student records would require sensitive operational data.

rejected.title: Office documents and routine follow-up
rejected.reason: The notice broadly names organizing documents, mail, archiving and checking routines, but establishes no frequency, document format or narrow automation boundary.

rejected.title: Document and mail administration
rejected.reason: The listed document registration, mail and office administration overlaps generic clerk duties but supplies too little detail to define a supported, distinct small workflow.

rejected.title: Administrator vacancy without task details
rejected.reason: The fresh text gives no task excerpt at all; its broad job category cannot support invented duties or task-specific demand evidence.

rejected.title: Invoice and order-flow administration
rejected.reason: The notice names invoicing and order flows but does not explain the process or inputs; existing refusals for invoice administration and this narrow evidence limit make it weaker than the separately assessed repair-shop task.

steps.message: Reviewed all 12 selected demand leads. One concrete repair-administration task was scored, but its mean is 4.4, below the threshold of 6; the remaining notices were excluded for broad, missing or previously refused chores. No post proposed.
